newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Independent agency urges compromise on Bosnia town.
newsitem.headline: Independent agency urges compromise on Bosnia town.

text.p: The disputed Bosnian town of Brcko should be ruled by the country's new inter-ethnic government and not be awarded to either Serb or Moslem-Croat authorities, an independent agency said on Wednesday.
The International Crisis Group, a private organisation monitoring the peace process in Bosnia, made the suggestion in a report urging compromise on the explosive issue of Brcko.
The London-based ICG proposed putting it under international administration for 18 months prior to it being transferred to the authority of Bosnia's peacetime central government.
"We believe this would be the only practical, legal and equitable way in which conflict could be avoided on this matter," Harian Balian, director of the ICG's Bosnia mission, told a news conference.

The future status of the strategic northern town was left unresolved in the Bosnian peace agreement. An arbitration panel led by a U.S. lawyer is supposed to deliver a decision on Brcko by a February 15 deadline.
Separatist Serb forces seized the town, 120 km (75 miles) north of Sarajevo, early in the Bosnian conflict and expelled its Moslem and Croat population which formed a majority there before the war.
The narrow Brcko land corridor links Bosnian Serb territory to the west and east and the Serbs have threatened to go to war to keep it inside their autonomous Serb republic.
The Moslem-Croat federation, which together with the Serb republic comprises peacetime Bosnia, says the Brcko area should go to the federation based on the pre-war ethnic population.
Awarding the town exclusively to either entity would risk another conflict and likely fail to restore the municipality's mixed population, the ICG said.

The ICG, a private non-profit organisation, is run by trustees, including prominent former government officials and policy makers. It was formed in 1995 seeking to draw attention to impending crises and avert "man-made" humanitarian disasters.
The agency also proposed the arbitration panel's mandate should be extended for five more years to provide a way of enforcing its decision on Brcko and bolstering any international administration.
During the five-year period, Bosnian factions would have the right to appeal to the panel in cases of "egregious violations" of the panel's decision or international law, Balian said.
Expanding the panel's jurisdiction would be a "potent weapon" and a key to making any solution work, he added.
"Otherwise the decision will remain on paper and will not be implemented in good faith or in full."
Under ICG's plan, an international governorship -- backed by international police -- would concentrate on returning refugees to pre-war homes and creating a duty-free zone in the area.
Balian warned that major powers were considering giving the town to Bosnia's Serb republic, which he said would reward "genocide" and risk another conflict.
"I think the international community is looking for an easy way out of the Brcko dilemma," Balian said.
